metadata.title: ChronoScope: Forecasting Methods, Sequence Diagnostics and Corpus Forecastability
metadata.description:
ChronoScope combines inspectable sequence diagnostics with explicit forecasting experiments. This revision adds exact Matrix Profile motifs and discords, FLUSS candidate segmentation, multiscale sample entropy, binary Lempel-Ziv complexity, time-reversal asymmetry and reproducibly seeded nonlinear fits. A separate fixed-protocol study processes all 4,227 M4 Daily identities: 4,226 are admitted and one is excluded for an unavailable scaled-error denominator. Forty features use only the earliest fitting prefix before three non-overlapping fourteen-step forecast blocks. Exact sequence identities allocate 2,946 discovery and 1,280 confirmation series. Kendall tests with dependent-test Benjamini-Yekutieli correction confirm 21 features under a fixed same-direction rule. Nevertheless, the discovery-trained selector has higher confirmation mean MASE than the discovery-selected AutoETS constant, 3.3501 versus 3.2570; the future-informed oracle gives 3.0005. This negative selection result is retained. The separate fresh twenty-two-variant experiment on fifteen selected cases also retains the negative ContextMemory comparison, mean MASE 1.4504 versus 1.4489 for RecencyMean. Source-bound artifacts, normative schemas, generated browser types and fourteen executed bilingual lessons expose the protocols and their limits. Related corpus sources, bounded model rosters, retrospective diagnostic scope, fixed training configurations and unverified pretrained-data overlap preclude population-superiority or operational-benefit claims.

Source code and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_ChronoScope . Research atlas: https://chronoscope.fasl-work.com . Not peer reviewed.
metadata.version_notes: Adds original-axis sequence diagnostics, reproducible nonlinear estimates, complete M4 Daily forecastability inference and the negative held-out method-selection result. Retains prior forecasting and combination evidence.
